'''Backup and Restore''' records the verified operations facts for the toolbox
<code>backup</code>, <code>restore_backup</code> and <code>checkpoint</code>
scripts. The scripts live in the toolbox service directory in the omni-root repo
and are also baked into the toolbox image; the baked copy can lag the repo copy.

== Backup flow ==

The backup script runs five steps plus a git-sync step:

# Copy the environment file into the data credentials directory.
# Dump the OmniAgent PostgreSQL database (custom format).
# Dump the Mattermost PostgreSQL database.
# Snapshot the Grafana SQLite database.
# Sync the artifacts to object storage.
# Git sync as the final step, through the omniagent sync endpoint.

Restore runs the git sync as its '''first''' step, before any service is stopped.
Both scripts guard on the agent container being up: when it is not running they
log <code>SKIPPING git sync</code> instead of starting it just to sync. Sync
errors are fail-soft - a warning, and the backup or restore continues.

== Object storage ==

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! Fact !! Detail
|-
| Credentials || <code>S3_ACCESS_KEY</code> and <code>S3_SECRET_KEY</code> in the stack environment file
|-
| Write capability || The key CAN write; a full upload was verified file by file
|-
| Expected 403 || Listing the bucket root is denied even with a write key; the project prefix is fully writable and readable
|-
| Authorization check || Call the provider authorization API and read the granted capabilities
|}

== Grafana caveat ==

The Grafana image ships no SQLite binary, so an old step that shelled out to
<code>sqlite3</code> inside the container exited 127 silently and produced no
snapshot while the container itself stayed healthy. The fix copies the database
file out of the container and snapshots it with the toolbox python3 SQLite backup
API. The fix is in the repo copy, and the running image still executes the old
baked script until the next toolbox image build, so run the fixed copy directly
until then.

== Checkpoint ==

The checkpoint script writes file data and a compressed database dump to a dated
prefix in object storage. A vector-store snapshot step is skipped when that
service is not deployed in the compose stack. Two caveats: the script exits 0
even when a copy step errors, so check the output per step, and two concurrent
runs race on the same temporary dump file - never launch two at once.

== Scheduled backups ==

The backup and checkpoint cron variables in the stack environment file are empty,
so no backup or checkpoint runs on a schedule. The git-sync step inside the backup
script is the only automated git persistence.

== Restoring a production dump into the dev stack ==

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! Step !! Fact
|-
| Source dump || The production PostgreSQL dump under the live data backups directory
|-
| Trap || A small seed dump under the workspace checkout is NOT production; restoring it silently yields a toy database
|-
| Commands || Stop the dev agent, recreate the database, restore with a matching-version client, start the agent again
|-
| Client version || The restore MUST run in a container whose client matches the dump archive version; an older client rejects it
|-
| Benign error || One unrecognized configuration parameter can make the restore exit non-zero while the restore is actually complete
|-
| Verify || Count threads, messages, secrets and tasks in the dev database and compare against production scale
|}

After restoring into a stack with a fresh Mattermost, the Setup endpoint alone
re-provisions its own team and channel, but any other channel bound in the
channel configuration must still be created on the server and re-pointed; a
restore that skips that reconciliation produces authorization errors on every
post in those channels. See [[Container Mount Map]] for the source and live paths
involved, [[Deployment Checklist]] for the deploy steps that surround a restore,
and [[Trinity Deploy]] for the release cycle that consumes a forced production
backup.
